promo-ebook-export.title: Stop exporting ebooks as PDF Print #shorts
promo-ebook-export.description:
Canva's own help pages: PDF Standard is "for multi-page and text-heavy documents" and you use it "if you intend to share your file through email". PDF Print is "for printing".

An ebook is read on a screen. 300 DPI buys nothing a screen can show — a screen cannot display more than about 96 DPI anyway.

What it does cost you is a file of tens of megabytes, and a buyer on mobile data watching a download bar that is not moving.

promo-ebook-flatten.title: Flatten PDF kills your contents page #shorts
promo-ebook-flatten.description:
On a pitch deck, Flatten PDF is exactly right — it stops people editing your file and locks your fonts.

On an ebook it costs you two things. Canva says flattening "may increase file size, especially with high-resolution images". And it turns your pages into images, so every link you built — the whole contents page, every back-to-contents — stops working.

The page looks identical. Nothing in it is clickable.

promo-ebook-contents.title: Make your PDF contents page actually jump #shorts
promo-ebook-contents.description:
Select the chapter line, hit the link button, and here is the part people miss: you are not linking to a website. In the link box, CHOOSE THE PAGE. Canva offers you the pages in this design.

Now the reader can jump. That is the difference between a document somebody opens once and a reference somebody keeps.

Build the contents page LAST — links point at page numbers, so inserting a page shifts everything below it.

promo-ebook-cover.title: Your ebook cover is seen at thumbnail size #shorts
promo-ebook-cover.description:
On a storefront your cover is a thumbnail a couple of centimetres across. The elegant thin serif and the three-line subtitle that look beautiful at full size turn into grey mush.

So build it, then shrink it on screen to about the size of a postage stamp and look. If you cannot read the title, it is not finished.

Fewer words, heavier type, more contrast than feels comfortable. A cover is a sign, not a page.
